title: An Indian-Origin CEO Just Raised $800 Million to Challenge Big Tech's AI Monopoly
excerpt: Noida-born Vipul Ved Prakash's Together AI has more than doubled its valuation to $8.3 billion, with annual bookings crossing $1.15 billion — all on the back of open-source models.
body:
Together AI, the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence startup founded by Indian-origin entrepreneur Vipul Ved Prakash, announced on Wednesday that it has raised $800 million in a Series C round led by Saudi Arabia's Aramco Ventures, catapulting its valuation to $8.3 billion — more than double the $3.3 billion it was worth just 18 months ago.

The round drew participation from Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, Salesforce Ventures, March Capital, Pegatron and SentinelOne's S Ventures. It marks Together AI as one of the highest-valued AI infrastructure companies in the world — and its founder as one of the most successful Indian-origin entrepreneurs in the current AI wave.

## From Noida to Silicon Valley

Prakash's story begins in the computer lab of Apeejay School in Noida, where a 12-year-old Vipul wrote his first program in BASIC — a simple script that asked for your name and replied with a greeting. "It still gives me goosebumps," he has said of that moment, which sparked a lifelong fascination with the idea that machines could exhibit intelligence.

After studying at IIT Delhi, Prakash moved to the United States, where he built a career across internet infrastructure, cybersecurity and privacy technology before founding Together AI in 2022 with a thesis that would prove prescient: the future of artificial intelligence would not be owned by a handful of closed-source giants but built by millions of developers using open models.

## The Anti-OpenAI Play

While OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have bet on proprietary, closed-source systems, Together AI has positioned itself as the infrastructure layer for open-source AI. Its platform lets companies train, fine-tune and deploy workloads on open models like DeepSeek, MiniMax and Kimi — often at significantly lower costs than running equivalent tasks on closed systems.

The business case has proved out decisively. Annual bookings crossed $1.15 billion last quarter, up from roughly $100 million in annualised revenue just a year ago. The platform now serves over a million registered developers and counts firms such as Cursor, Cognition, Decagon, Salesforce, Zoom and The Washington Post among its customers.

"The future of AI won't be owned by a few companies. It will be built by millions of developers and businesses, and open-source models are making that possible," Prakash said in a statement.

## A 50-Fold Infrastructure Expansion

Together AI said it would use the fresh capital to widen its offerings as it expands from primarily a training platform to a full-stack provider of inference — the computationally intensive process of running trained AI models at scale. The company expects its computing capacity and infrastructure to expand roughly 50-fold over the next five years.

The scale of that ambition is underscored by the investors. Aramco Ventures, the venture capital arm of the world's largest oil company, has been aggressively diversifying into AI and digital infrastructure. Nvidia, which supplies the GPUs that power Together AI's clusters, participated for the third consecutive round. Vista Equity Partners, the enterprise software-focused fund, signals institutional confidence in Together AI's enterprise traction.

The startup has also secured 20 gigawatts of power generation capacity to support new AI clusters. One upcoming cluster is set to feature 36,000 of Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 chips — each containing two CPUs and four Blackwell B200 GPUs — positioning Together AI alongside the largest AI compute buildouts globally.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

Prakash joins a growing roster of Indian-origin founders leading some of the most consequential AI companies in the world. OpenAI just appointed Prabhjeet Singh, Uber's India head, to run its second-largest market. Satya Nadella steers Microsoft's AI strategy. Sundar Pichai leads Google's AI push. And now Prakash, who coded his first program in a Noida school, commands an $8.3 billion platform that sits at the centre of the open-source AI movement.

For Indian engineers and entrepreneurs in the AI space, Together AI's trajectory validates an alternative path — one built not on proprietary lock-in but on open models, distributed computing, and the conviction that the best AI infrastructure should be accessible to everyone. The company's Indian-origin leadership also connects it to a deep talent pipeline: India now produces more AI researchers than any country outside the United States, and Together AI's platform is increasingly used by Indian startups building on open-source models.

The Series C round brings Together AI's total funding to over $1.4 billion. At an $8.3 billion valuation, it sits among the top 10 most valuable AI startups globally — and its founder's journey from Noida to Silicon Valley's front rank has only just begun.

*Sources: Reuters, Forbes India, VentureBeat, LinkedIn*
